causes.finding: Composite reservation cards include category/date/place/status in one fixed label. The lexical apply score is 60 minus 15 for label length >36 =45, below55. The separate card-title fallback expects a direct title then p, unlike the actual div/strong/div/span shape.
city-reservation-help is selected as apply; accepted category is help. Broad reservation text wins without a guide interpretation.

city-login navigate vs accepted locate; city-reservation-help locate vs accepted navigate. Plain HTTP login has no explicit handler, while reservation help has role=button/aria-controls/aria-haspopup. Existing sourceAction deterministically explains both outputs. This requires separate policy/annotation review; do not classify both as demonstrated engine defects or change this first result.

All8 extracted candidates produce0 classified. Expected stage controls are sibling buttons in div.tab-area, rather than ul/ol/tablist. They have aria-expanded but their short phase labels do not satisfy the supplemental panel group label-suffix guards. The generic contextual-help branch supports questions/handoffs, not these phase tabs. A page-purpose signal alone intentionally cannot classify every link.

Purpose detection only uses selected pathname tokens, selected semantic heading locations, and eligible preceding context. Unclassified candidates do not log their derived purpose/context, so this diagnosis does not claim which context label was produced at runtime. Even a help purpose does not bypass the missing specific-control evidence path.

lib-result-guide and lib-search-guide are selected as search, but accepted category is help. The expected result guide source is present on screen yet fails expected matching because its category differs.

The group-slide source has role=group and locate action, but its visible preceding title is a subject title, not a guide title ending 안내. Supplemental group help requires guideContext; collection fallback expects list/tablist structure. The generic detail label and download button therefore have no qualifying help path.

The full-guide control is a button. isDocumentDownload recognizes anchors only, and there is no explicit generic guide-button classification. Its safe locate action is available, but it is not classified.

All3 expected functions match. The extra search input has a safe fixed label but no evaluation sourceId; accepted search source is the separate search button. It is counted incorrect and also leaves1 unresolved menuFlow source mapping. This is a real original control, not evidence that an absent function was invented.

nps-login is classified login but navigate vs accepted locate. Source is a plain HTTP anchor with no explicit handler. sourceAction explains navigate; separately adjudicate the authentication-entry contract without overwriting this first result.

The2 accepted non-required detail/help links are not classified. Their fixed visible name is generic detail, while card subject lives in sibling item-info/strong and title. Safe label extraction prefers visible text over title; card fallback only supports title/paragraph inside the control.

All7 candidate controls are extracted, only login classified. Primary academic lexical rules omit the actual major-system concepts; academic concept fallbacks additionally require a qualifying academic context. Tab links precede the page h4 in a sibling content section, and preceding scoped-heading extraction cannot use that later title. No site-specific URL endpoint is recognized.

Expected cross-path fragment links are annotated locate, but sourceAction only treats same-document fragment URLs as locate. If these sources later classify, their action requires separate contract review. No selected SMU academic action was evaluated in this report.

menuFlow.interpretation: Additional-menu traversal only exposes classified overflow. Here it adds no expected coverage and cannot substitute for first-screen quality. It proves fixture UI display/source matching only, not action activation or installed-extension/user task success.
